newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rebhold buys HoneyFields, other deals due.
newsitem.headline: Rebhold buys HoneyFields, other deals due.

text.p: Recently listed food, freight and liquor group Rebhold Ltd on Monday said that it had bought Gauteng-based HoneyFields.
The deal was subject to the completion of a due diligence investigation, Rebhold said in a statement.
Rebhold on Monday also issued another cautionary statement that it was involved in further negotiations on other acquisitions which could affect the price of its shares.
HoneyFields, founded by George Lee-Georghiou in 1990, manufactures and distributes the largest range of wafers and sugar cones in South Africa.

The purchase price would be fixed on a formula which would result in Rebhold paying 4.3 times the average annualised after-tax profits achieved by HoneyFields in the 30 months from the effective date of the transaction.
Rebhold would make the purchase by allotting and issuing between 6.5 million and a maximum of 9.1 million Rebhold shares in three tranches.
Rebhold chief executive Jaques Kempen said the deal would not have a material effect on earnings or net asset value for the year to June 30, 1997.
He said there was considerable potential for further expansion in the marketing and production of HoneyFields' products to the retail industry and for export.
